question: What is the primary function of a syringe driver in clinical practice?

options.A: Providing high-pressure oxygen therapy to lungs
options.B: Measuring hourly urine output in critical patients
options.C: Rapidly replacing large volumes of lost blood
options.D: Delivering continuous and precise medication infusion

explanation: The device is specifically engineered to administer small, exact volumes of liquid medication continuously over time. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why is a syringe driver preferred over intermittent bolus injections for continuous pain management?

options.A: It completely eliminates all potential adverse drug reactions
options.B: It requires zero monitoring by nursing staff during the shift
options.C: It maintains stable therapeutic drug levels without peaks and troughs
options.D: It allows patients to adjust their own dosage without limits

explanation: Continuous infusion prevents the cycle of high drug levels followed by pain breakthrough that happens with intermittent dosing. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h1)

question: What is the preferred route for administering medications via syringe driver in palliative care?
explanation: Subcutaneous infusion is the standard choice for chronic symptom control because it is less invasive and easier to maintain than IV access. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h2)

question: A patient with severe dysphagia and terminal bowel obstruction requires continuous analgesia. What makes a syringe driver appropriate here?

options.A: Oral medications cannot be safely swallowed or absorbed
options.B: It allows the patient to walk around the ward without help
options.C: It removes the need to monitor vital signs every four hours
options.D: Intramuscular injections are too effective for chronic pain

explanation: When the gastrointestinal tract is compromised, alternative parenteral routes using a driver bypass the gut entirely. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h2)

question: What component of the syringe driver pushes the plunger forward to deliver the medication?
explanation: The pusher block is the mechanical arm that engages with the syringe plunger and moves it at a controlled rate. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h3)

question: What is the clinical role of the occlusion sensor on a syringe driver?

options.A: Detecting pressure increases caused by blockages in the line
options.B: Warning staff when the battery is running low on power
options.C: Measuring the exact volume of fluid remaining in the barrel
options.D: Checking if the correct brand of syringe has been loaded

explanation: The occlusion sensor triggers an alarm when resistance rises, preventing fluid backup or tissue infiltration. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h3)

question: Why must a nurse check drug compatibility before preparing a multi-drug syringe driver mixture?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing extra equipment
options.B: To prevent chemical precipitation and loss of drug efficacy
options.C: To make sure the total volume fits inside a standard syringe
options.D: To ensure the infusion finishes exactly at the end of the shift

explanation: Incompatible drugs can react chemically, forming visible particles or crystals that clog the line and render the treatment useless. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h4)

question: Which action is a mandatory safety check prior to starting a syringe driver infusion?

options.A: Warming the medication to body temperature with hot water
options.B: Placing the device in a locked cabinet away from the bed
options.C: Priming the extension tubing with sterile tap water
options.D: Verifying the prescription against the patient chart

explanation: Double-checking the order against the patient profile prevents administration errors and ensures right-patient, right-drug delivery. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h4)

question: Why is priming the extension tubing before connecting it to the patient essential?

options.A: To remove all air bubbles and prevent air embolism
options.B: To test if the syringe barrel can withstand pressure
options.C: To warm up the plastic tubing for patient comfort
options.D: To verify that the medication color is bright and clear

explanation: Clearing air from the line ensures that only liquid medication enters the patient's subcutaneous space or vein. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h5)

question: What is the purpose of performing a dual-nurse check on the programmed rate?

options.A: Ensuring the battery charger is plugged into the wall
options.B: Complying with hospital policies regarding nursing shifts
options.C: Speeding up the time it takes to set up the equipment
options.D: Catching programming errors before the infusion begins

explanation: Having a second colleague verify the math and rate reduces the risk of dangerous over-infusion or under-infusion. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h5)

question: How often should the nurse inspect the subcutaneous infusion site of a running syringe driver?
explanation: Regular inspection allows early detection of localized complications like inflammation, swelling, or site leakage. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h6)

question: A patient complains of localized pain and swelling around the subcutaneous needle site. What is the appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Increase the infusion rate to push the fluid through faster
options.B: Administer an oral painkiller and leave the needle in place
options.C: Wrap a tight bandage around the site to stop the swelling
options.D: Stop the infusion and assess the site for infiltration

explanation: Pain and swelling indicate the fluid is leaking into the surrounding tissue instead of absorbing properly, requiring site relocation. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h6)

question: What is the first action a nurse should take when a syringe driver sounds an occlusion alarm?

options.A: Disconnect the battery and restart the machine
options.B: Inspect the entire tubing line for kinks or clogs
options.C: Remove the needle and switch to oral medication
options.D: Increase the pressure limit setting on the device

explanation: An occlusion alarm signals a blockage, which is frequently caused by a simple physical kink in the extension set. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common cause of a syringe driver occlusion alarm?

options.D: A closed roller clamp on the set

explanation: A dead or low battery triggers a distinct power alarm, whereas occlusion alarms specifically relate to fluid pathway blockages. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h7)

question: What details must be recorded in the nursing notes when starting a syringe driver?

options.A: Patient favorite food and visitors present
options.B: Drug name, dose, rate, and site location
options.C: Cost of the consumables used for the setup
options.D: Brand name of the pump manufacturing company

explanation: Comprehensive documentation must include the specific medication details, administration rate, and anatomical site for clinical continuity and safety. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h8)

question: Why is strict aseptic technique crucial when preparing and managing a syringe driver?

options.A: To prevent introduction of pathogens and local or systemic infection
options.B: To comply with manufacturer warranty rules for the pump
options.C: To make sure the digital screen remains clean and readable
options.D: To ensure the battery retains its charge for a longer time

explanation: Parenteral administration bypasses normal skin barriers, making infection control essential to protect vulnerable patients from sepsis. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h8)
